steps.message:
This is a one-character-class change, but it's a breaking change to a published interface, so I want a yes before touching it.

`routes/users.js:6` returns `userId` to three consumers named in `README.md:3` — the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export. Renaming it to `user_id` breaks every one of them until they ship a matching update; the iOS clients in particular can't be updated in lockstep. The README also states the project's own rule: "Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint."

So the consistency argument is real (`/orders` at line 12 is already snake_case), but the straight rename is the one option the repo's stated policy rules out.

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Add user_id alongside userId in the /users response. Non-breaking: existing clients keep working, new clients can adopt snake_case. Remove userId later once the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the partner export have all migrated.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: What the README prescribes: leave /users as-is and add a v2 route that returns user_id. Most faithful to the stated contract policy, but the largest change - new route, wiring, and a migration path for consumers.

options.label: Rename it anyway
options.description: Straight rename of the single field at routes/users.js:6, accepting the break. Only if you already know all three consumers are updated or the contract note is stale.
